title: "I Am Not Ordering You to Attack"
text:
On the morning of April 25, 1915, Australian and New Zealand troops landed on the Gallipoli peninsula as part of the Allied attempt to force the Dardanelles and knock the Ottoman Empire out of the war. They pushed inland toward the high ridges that commanded the whole area.

Mustafa Kemal, then a lieutenant colonel commanding the Ottoman 19th Division in reserve, went forward to see for himself. By his own later account, he met a group of Ottoman soldiers retreating from the heights because they had run out of ammunition, with the enemy following. He ordered them to fix bayonets and lie down facing the enemy, which made the advancing troops pause and take cover. Then he brought up his 57th Infantry Regiment.

As he sent them into the attack, he recalled telling them: "I am not ordering you to attack. I am ordering you to die. In the time it takes us to die, other troops and commanders can come and take our places."

The 57th Regiment was almost entirely destroyed, but the counterattacks held the heights, and the Allies never broke through. The campaign ended with their evacuation in January 1916. The Turkish army has never formed another 57th Regiment.
lesson: In a crisis, being honest about what a task will cost, and why it matters, can hold people together better than false reassurance.
source: Mustafa Kemal's later account of the Anafartalar and Ariburnu battles, recorded in his memoirs and interviews
caveat: The order is known from Mustafa Kemal's own later recollection rather than from a written order of the day.
